# daymath

> ISO 8601 calendar day math for JavaScript. date-fns-shaped function names. Temporal.PlainDate under the hood. No silent local now. A Date or a time zone enters through day() and nowhere else.

## Links

- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/daymath
- Source: https://github.com/leemr/daymath
- Playground: https://leemr.github.io/daymath/
- Changelog: https://github.com/leemr/daymath/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md
- Contributing: https://github.com/leemr/daymath/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
- Future / backlog: https://github.com/leemr/daymath/blob/master/FUTURE.md
- Types: https://github.com/leemr/daymath/blob/master/index.d.ts
- Implementation: https://github.com/leemr/daymath/blob/master/index.js

## Install

```bash
npm install daymath
```

```js
import { day, addDays, differenceInDays, isSameDay } from 'daymath'
```

## Contract

- Inputs: ISO day string `YYYY-MM-DD` or expanded `±YYYYYY-MM-DD`, or Temporal.PlainDate from any implementation
- Range: `-271821-04-19` … `+275760-09-13` (Temporal PlainDate limit); outside it throws RangeError
- Outputs: ISO day strings (Temporal toString form)
- Date objects: TypeError on every public path including isValid(Date), except day()
- day(moment?, tz?): the calendar day of a moment, in a zone. Defaults are stated: moment is now, zone is 'utc'. moment accepts Date, epoch MILLISECONDS (as new Date(n) reads it), ISO day string, PlainDate, or an ISO timestamp carrying Z or an offset. A day carries no time so a zone does not apply to it. A string carrying a [Zone] annotation names its own zone, keeps its own civil day, and ignores the UTC default; passing tz as well throws. '11/12/2026' and '2026-08-08T12:00' (no offset and no zone, so daymath would have to pick) are refused; '2026-08-08T12:00[America/New_York]' is accepted. A lone string takes one of four roles in this order: day, zoned time, instant, then zone; the zone test is by shape (an IANA name, which carries no colon, or a bare offset like +05:30). A calendar annotation naming iso8601 is accepted and dropped, in any case. Any other calendar is judged where it is APPLIED — with a zone bracket, and on a day string — and it is ACCEPTED when it only relabels the year, so day('2026-08-08T12:00[America/New_York][u-ca=buddhist]') answers '2026-08-08[u-ca=buddhist]'. A calendar that renumbers months or days is refused. Without a zone bracket the string names an Instant, which has no fields for a calendar to renumber, so '2026-08-08T20:00:00Z[u-ca=buddhist]' is answered with the annotation dropped. Only export that reads a clock; only door a Date enters by. Never returns a Date, never stores the zone.
- Calendars: a `[u-ca=…]` annotation is ACCEPTED when the calendar only relabels the year, and REFUSED when it renumbers months or days. The line is measured at runtime, never held as a list, so a calendar CLDR adds later needs no code change: the month and day must equal the ISO fields and the year offset must be constant, checked on nine probe dates from 1900 to 2100 with two pairs straddling a Japanese era boundary. Today that accepts buddhist (+543), roc (−1911), japanese (0) and gregory (0), and refuses the other twelve the runtime can build. The annotation rides along, so getYear('2026-01-31[u-ca=buddhist]') is 2569 and addDays gives '2026-02-01[u-ca=buddhist]'. iso8601 is accepted and dropped rather than carried. The rule reads Temporal, not Intl: Intl reports the ERA year, Reiwa 8 and B.R.O.C. 12, where Temporal reports a continuous year. Needs temporal-polyfill/full, which costs 4.2 kB gzip and buys identical answers on runtimes without native Temporal.
- Mixed calendar pair: a day is the same day whatever its year is labelled, so measurement normalises both sides to ISO instead of throwing. differenceInDays('2026-03-01', '2026-01-31[u-ca=buddhist]') is 29, and isEqual('2026-01-31[u-ca=buddhist]', '2026-01-31') is true. Temporal's own since and until refuse this with `Mismatched calendars`. Only exports that read or write a field honour the label.
- A Temporal STRING's date part is always ISO, so '2026-01-31[u-ca=buddhist]' is the same day as '2026-01-31'. The FIELDS form is different: from({year:2026, calendar:'buddhist'}) is ISO 1483-01-31, 543 years away. daymath takes strings and PlainDate objects, never the fields form, so it inherits Temporal's rule.
- isValid(badString): false
- getMonth/setMonth: 1–12 ISO (1=January), NOT date-fns 0-based; getDay: 1=Monday…7=Sunday ISO, NOT date-fns 0=Sunday; weekStartsOn default 7, 0 also accepted for Sunday
- differenceInMonths counts a month as full when addMonths would carry the earlier date to the later one, so 2026-01-31 to 2026-02-28 is 1; differenceInMonths(addMonths(d,n),d) === n always holds
- isSameDay is an alias of isEqual
- format only supports pattern yyyy-MM-dd (identity normalize); not locale display
- Intervals: { start, end }; areIntervalsOverlapping defaults inclusive false like date-fns

## When to use

- Pure calendar storage and math (hire date, trip day, passport day as strings)
- Swapping date-fns *names* while keeping string days (not a drop-in for Date-based code)

## When not to use

- Display formats like "MMM d" — use Temporal toLocaleString or date-fns
- Zoned times or instant math — use Temporal Instant/ZonedDateTime; day() converts an instant to a day but keeps no time

## PRs

Fork and open a pull request. Do not expect direct push access. See CONTRIBUTING.md. Keep 100% coverage on index.js.
